For Becky & Kit · July 24 – August 2, 2026

Argentina.

Five nights in Buenos Aires, two beside the falls in Iguazú, with a UNESCO-listed colonial-town day across the river to Uruguay. The pace is unhurried, the lodging is hand-picked, and the days weave both travelers' priorities: Becky's love of art, gardens, and wildlife with Kit's anchors at El Ateneo, MALBA, Casa Brandon, and Teatro Colón. Buenos Aires bookended by an overnight in each direction from San Diego.

Return San DiegoSunday, August 2 · morning

The journey, day by day

Travel
Friday, July 24 · leaving San Diego

Evening departure from SAN — connect at Dallas, then the overnight to Buenos Aires (EZE). You sleep through the cabin lights and wake somewhere over Brazil. The 24th and 25th collapse into one long arc of flying.

Day 1
Saturday, July 25 · bienvenidos a Buenos Aires

Land EZE in the morning, after the overnight from Dallas. Slip through customs and settle into Palo Santo Hotel — a 26-room boutique in Palermo Hollywood, draped in vertical gardens. Lunch on a leafy side street. A long walk through the neighborhood. An early Argentine dinner.

Day 2
Sunday, July 26 · gardens and modern art

A quiet morning in the Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays, the 1890s gardens designed by the French landscape architect — and the adjacent Jardín Japonés, a small ticketed garden right next door. After lunch, MALBA for Frida Kahlo's Diego y yo and the continent's most important Latin American collection. If energy allows, an early-evening walk on the Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur river-edge wetland.

Day 3
Monday, July 27 · Dante and a bookstore in a theater

A morning tour of Palacio Barolo, the 1923 building designed around Dante's Divine Comedy, ending at the rooftop lighthouse. (Book the bilingual or evening tour — only those reach the lighthouse.) In the afternoon, a short ride to El Ateneo Grand Splendid in Recoleta — the 1919 grand theater reborn as a bookstore, with frescoed ceilings and reading nooks where the opera boxes used to be.

Day 4
Tuesday, July 28 · a day in Uruguay

Colonia del Sacramento, a one-hour fast ferry across the Río de la Plata. The UNESCO-listed Barrio Histórico is twelve walkable blocks of cobblestones and 17th-century Portuguese-then-Spanish architecture — the Calle de los Suspiros, the Puerta de la Ciudadela drawbridge, the lighthouse with its 110-step climb, the rambla along the river. Lunch at a Plaza Mayor café. Late-afternoon ferry back.

Day 5
Wednesday, July 29 · a day on your own terms

Mornings split. Becky takes the Mitre train to Tigre Delta — the river-town market, a short delta boat ride, lunch on the waterfront. Kit gets the solo Palermo morning — coffee, a bookshop, a long wander. Reconvene mid-afternoon for the Teatro Colón English tour, one of the five great opera houses of the world. Dinner. The evening at Casa Brandon, the queer cultural center named for Brandon Teena — film, books, art, a small bar. Optional late drop-in at Mundo Lingo, the multilingual social where conversation starts by the flag on your name tag.

Day 6
Thursday, July 30 · north to the jungle

Morning flight to Iguazú. Gran Meliá Iguazú is the only hotel inside the Argentine national park — 183 rooms with rainforest at the windows, eye-level access to the park itself. The Upper Circuit trail begins on the property: a 1,750-meter loop with no stairs, the gentle introduction. Afternoon walk-out for the first views.

Day 7
Friday, July 31 · the rainforest in full

Gran Meliá guests get a private hour in the park at 7 AM, before the gates open to day visitors — the best window for wildlife. Coatis are everywhere (ring-tailed, raccoon-cousin, persistent — don't feed them). Capuchin monkeys in the canopy on the Lower Circuit. Toucans at dawn, if you're lucky. Two thousand species of butterflies, no exaggeration. Mid-day: Devil's Throat by ecological train, the cinematic U-shaped chasm taking half the river's flow. Late afternoon: the pool, or Sendero Macuco for one more forest walk.

Day 8
Saturday, August 1 · the slow morning, the long flight

A late breakfast, then the midday flight to Buenos Aires (AEP), a transfer to Ezeiza (EZE), and the evening overnight back to Dallas. You spend the night in the air.

Travel
Sunday, August 2 · home

The overnight from Buenos Aires lands in Dallas at dawn; final connection puts you back in San Diego mid-morning. Plan a quiet Sunday — BA is only 4 hours ahead of SD, so the time-zone hit is light, but the overnight is still an overnight.

Must-do this week

Lock the trip in. Everything else sequences out over the next six weeks.

  • Confirm both passports valid through February 2027 — renew now if close (routine processing is 6–8 weeks). Both passports work for Uruguay too — same passport, just a stamp.
  • Book the flights — SAN → DFW → EZE on American, single ticket, premium economy or business class. Confirm August 1 EZE → DFW is operating (American's summer EZE service runs May 21 – Aug 3, 2026).
  • Reserve Palo Santo Hotel for July 25–30 — request an upper floor or garden-facing room.
  • Reserve Gran Meliá Iguazú for July 30 – August 1 — request a park-view room; ask about the airport transfer when booking.
  • Buy Argentine travel health insurance ($30K+ medical/evacuation; required at entry under Decree 366/2025, in force since July 2025).

Day-by-day in detail

Times, addresses, what to know.

Friday, July 24 · departure from San Diego

  • Evening flight SAN → DFW on American.
  • Connect in Dallas (target a ~3-hour layover — long enough to eat, short enough not to drag).
  • Overnight DFW → EZE on American 787. Lights out for most of the cabin.
  • You will not get a real night of sleep, even in business class — pack accordingly.

Saturday, July 25 · arrival in Buenos Aires

  • Land EZE in the morning. Uber to Palermo Hollywood (~45 min, ~$30–50). Walk past the unmarked-taxi touts to the official Uber pickup.
  • Check into Palo Santo Hotel (Bonpland 2275, Palermo Hollywood). Pay with a non-Argentine card to automatically waive the 21% VAT — confirm with passport at check-in. A small ~$1.50/night Buenos Aires city tax still applies.
  • Lunch nearby. Nap. Easy walk.
  • Early dinner, early bed.

Sunday, July 26 · gardens & MALBA

  • 9 AM Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays — Av. Santa Fe 3951, walkable from the hotel. Free entry, quietest at opening, ~2 hours.
  • Jardín Japonés — Av. Casares 2966, adjacent to the botánico. Separate paid ticket (~ARS 13,500 non-residents).
  • Lunch in Palermo.
  • MALBA — Av. Figueroa Alcorta 3415. Open Thursday – Monday 12:00–20:00 (closed Tuesday and Wednesday). Frida's Diego y yo is on view in the Costantini collection. Two to three hours.
  • Optional late afternoon: Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur — Puerto Madero, the river-edge wetland. ~20 min Uber from MALBA.
  • Evening: Palermo dinner.

Monday, July 27 · Palacio Barolo & El Ateneo

  • Palacio Barolo — Av. de Mayo 1370, Monserrat. Book the bilingual daytime tour or the evening tour — those are the ones that reach the rooftop lighthouse. The Spanish-only daytime tour stops short. ~90 min. ~USD 30–35.
  • Lunch in Microcentro or along Avenida de Mayo.
  • El Ateneo Grand Splendid — Av. Santa Fe 1860, Recoleta. ~15 min Uber from Microcentro. The "Grand Splendid Experience" tells the building's history.
  • Optional evening: Escape Buenos Aires or Timbre 4 (see Add-ons).

Tuesday, July 28 · Colonia del Sacramento, Uruguay

  • Morning fast ferry from Puerto Madero. Three operators run the route: Colonia Express (5 sailings/day, often cheapest), Buquebus (3 sailings/day, largest), Seacat. Crossing is ~1h10. Earliest BA → Colonia is ~08:30; last return ~20:46.
  • Terminal: Av. Antártida Argentina 821, Buenos Aires (Buquebus terminal). Argentine exit and Uruguayan entry are both pre-cleared at the BA terminal before boarding — bring both passports.
  • From the Colonia ferry terminal it's a 15–20 minute walk to the Barrio Histórico.
  • On the ground: the cobblestone Calle de los Suspiros, the Puerta de la Ciudadela drawbridge, the Basílica del Santísimo Sacramento, Plaza Mayor cafés, the rambla riverfront. The Faro (lighthouse) is a 110-step climb with a small cash-only fee (~$3–5 USD).
  • Lunch in the old town. The whole historic district is twelve walkable blocks.
  • Late-afternoon ferry back to BA. Quiet dinner.

Wednesday, July 29 · split morning, Colón, Casa Brandon

  • Becky → Tigre Delta solo. Mitre line train from Retiro to Tigre, ~45–55 minutes, every 15–20 minutes during the day. Requires a SUBE card. Verify the Mitre line is operating before the trip (Trenes Argentinos site or Twitter/X) — service had recent disruptions in early 2026. Backup: Tren de la Costa from Olivos, or Uber direct (~45–60 min). At Tigre: the riverside Puerto de Frutos market, a 1-hour delta boat ride (Sturla, Interisleña), lunch on the water. Half-day budget, back mid-afternoon.
  • Kit → solo Palermo morning. Coffee, a bookshop, a long wander.
  • Reconvene for a late lunch in BA.
  • Teatro Colón English tour — Cerrito 628. English tours typically run at 11 AM, 12 PM, and 3 PM (~50 minutes, ~ARS 10,000). Book direct on the city site and pick "Inglés." Aim for the 3 PM slot to keep the morning unhurried.
  • Coffee back in Palermo.
  • 8 PM Casa Brandon — Luis María Drago 236, Villa Crespo. Open Wed–Sun, programming posts ~2 weeks out; confirm at brandon.org.ar or DM Instagram around July 15.
  • Optional 9 PM drop-in at Mundo Lingo at Baum Catrina, Palermo Soho (Wednesday session — no booking, name-tags-by-flag).

Thursday, July 30 · north to Iguazú

  • Morning flight AEP → IGR on Aerolíneas Argentinas (~1h45m). Leave bulk luggage at Palo Santo if returning; the hotel will hold it.
  • Gran Meliá Iguazú is ~10 km / ~20 minutes from the airport. The hotel arranges private transfers — request when booking.
  • Check-in. Request a park-view room. 183 rooms, 5-star — the only hotel inside the Argentine national park boundary.
  • Afternoon: the Upper Circuit trail begins at the property. 1,750 meters, no stairs, ~2 hours, the gentle introduction. Coatis on the path — they will approach; don't feed them.
  • Dinner at the hotel.

Friday, July 31 · Iguazú in full

  • 7 AM exclusive guest hour — Gran Meliá guests have the park to themselves for one hour before public opening. Best window for wildlife.
  • Morning: Lower Circuit (~1.7 km). Best dense-forest section — capuchin monkeys in the canopy, toucans at dawn (luck of the draw), butterflies in numbers.
  • Optional: Gran Aventura zodiac boat ride under the falls. Bring a waterproof phone pouch.
  • Lunch.
  • Mid-afternoon: Devil's Throat by ecological train from Cataratas Station (~8–10 min per segment, runs every 20–30 min). The cinematic U-shaped chasm taking half the river's flow.
  • Late afternoon: pool, spa, or Sendero Macuco for a final rainforest walk.
  • Evening at the hotel.

Saturday, August 1 · last morning in Argentina, evening flight out

  • Slow morning at Gran Meliá. The Upper Circuit is right there if you want one more look.
  • AR1777 11:00 IGR → AEP (or AR1779 12:45 if 11:00 unavailable).
  • Uber from AEP to EZE (60–90 minutes weekend afternoon).
  • Arrive EZE by ~3 PM for the evening international flight.
  • Evening EZE → DFW overnight. You spend the night in the air.

Sunday, August 2 · arrive home in San Diego

  • Overnight EZE → DFW lands in Dallas around dawn.
  • Morning connection DFW → SAN on American.
  • Arrive San Diego mid-morning.
  • You will be tired. Plan nothing for Sunday afternoon.

Lodging

Palo Santo Hotel — Buenos Aires

  • Bonpland 2275, Palermo Hollywood
  • 4-star boutique · 26 rooms · Booking 9.3/10
  • Vertical gardens soften street sound; quiet by design.
  • Request at booking: upper floor or garden-facing room.
  • Pay with a non-Argentine card to automatically waive the 21% VAT. Buenos Aires city tax of ~$1.50/night still applies.
  • Sources: palosantohotel.com · Booking.com

Gran Meliá Iguazú

  • Iguazú National Park, Misiones Province (nearest city Puerto Iguazú; ~10 km from IGR airport)
  • 5-star resort · 183 rooms · the only hotel inside the Argentine park boundary
  • Formerly Sheraton Iguazú (1978), then Meliá Iguazú, rebranded Gran Meliá in 2021.
  • Exclusive guest perk: 7 AM private park access, one hour before public opening — best window for wildlife and uncrowded photos.
  • Upper Circuit starts at the hotel (1,750 m loop, no stairs).
  • Devil's Throat is not walkable from the hotel — requires the ecological train from Cataratas Station.
  • Request: a park-view room. Ask the hotel about the airport transfer when booking.
  • Sources: melia.com · Wikipedia

Flights

International — primary

SAN → DFW → EZE on American Airlines, single PNR, both directions. Connection at Dallas; overnight 787 to Buenos Aires. ~3-hour DFW layover is the sweet spot.

American's seasonal EZE service runs May 21 – August 3, 2026 (4× weekly, 787-8). The August 1 EZE → DFW return is within the window — confirm the specific flight is operating before purchase.

International — alternates (if DFW sells out)

  • SAN → MIA → EZE on American — Miami is American's year-round EZE gateway.
  • SAN → ATL → EZE on Delta — Atlanta hub.
  • SAN → IAH → EZE on United — Houston hub.

Cabin

  • Premium Economy — the comfort floor for an overnight leg.
  • Business class — lie-flat seats, real sleep on the overnight.

Domestic — Buenos Aires ⇄ Iguazú

  • Aerolíneas Argentinas (the only carrier on this route).
  • Outbound: AEP → IGR Thursday July 30, morning.
  • Return: AR1777 11:00 IGR → AEP Saturday August 1 (or AR1779 12:45). Earlier is safer.

AEP and EZE are different airports. Domestic uses Aeroparque (AEP), in the city. International uses Ezeiza (EZE), 45 minutes south. The Saturday transfer between them takes 60–90 minutes; budget 3+ hours total from AEP arrival to EZE international check-in.

Practical

Passport & entry — Argentina

US citizens don't need a tourist visa for Argentina (≤90 days). Passport valid 6+ months past entry. Travel health insurance with $30K+ medical / evacuation coverage is required under Decree 366/2025 (in force since July 2025) and may be checked on arrival.

Passport & entry — Uruguay

Same passport. US citizens get visa-free entry for up to 90 days. Immigration is pre-cleared at the Buenos Aires ferry terminal — both Argentine exit and Uruguayan entry stamps before boarding.

Money

21% VAT on hotel stays is automatically waived for foreign tourists paying with a non-Argentine card (Buenos Aires city tax of ~$1.50/night still applies). Argentina's foreign-exchange controls were lifted in April 2025; all rates now within ~3% of each other. Foreign Visa or Mastercard wins for nearly everything; bring ~$100–150 USD cash for tips, the Colonia lighthouse fee, and small vendors.

Weather — Argentine winter

Buenos Aires: highs 12–15°C, lows 5–8°C, often damp. Warm coat, layers, rain jacket, sturdy walking shoes.

Iguazú: highs 20–23°C, lows 12–14°C, humid. Light rain layer essential — the falls spray is substantial. Waterproof phone pouch for the park.

Phones

T-Mobile and Verizon international plans work in both Argentina and Uruguay. WhatsApp is the default messaging app in Argentina — install/test on both phones before departure. Download offline maps of Palermo, Colonia, and Puerto Iguazú.

Iguazú — wildlife etiquette

Coatis are not pets. They will approach for food, can bite, and signs throughout the park warn against feeding. Keep snacks in zipped packs. They are also adorable, abundant, and the symbol of the park.

Iguazú timing note

Late July is peak Argentine winter school break (vacaciones de invierno). The park will be busier than off-season — which is exactly why Gran Meliá's 7 AM exclusive guest hour matters. Arrive at the gate at park opening, and time Devil's Throat for late afternoon when bus groups have cleared.

Tigre line status

The Mitre line had a reported repair closure earlier in 2026. Likely resolved by July, but verify on Trenes Argentinos before Wednesday. Backups: Tren de la Costa from Olivos, or Uber direct (~45–60 minutes).

Optional add-ons

Slottable without breaking the plan — choose a few, ignore the rest.

  • A quieter graduation dinner. Don Julio is the famous parrilla — and the wrong sensory environment (loud, packed, long line outside, tight tables). Better-fitting options:
    • Casa SaltShaker — puerta cerrada (closed-door) dinner in a host's home, 5-course shared table, intimate by design.
    • La Brigada — San Telmo parrilla with the same quality meat as Don Julio, half the price, calmer atmosphere.
    • Palo Santo Hotel's restaurant or a concierge-recommended neighborhood spot, with a "quiet table, low-stimulation" request at booking.
  • Escape Buenos Aires — Private bilingual escape room in Caballito. Slots into any free evening (Sun or Mon).
  • Timbre 4 — Acclaimed director Claudio Tolcachir's independent theater in Boedo. Check timbre4.com for English-subtitled productions in the window — slot any evening if a show fits.
  • Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes — Av. del Libertador 1473. Free admission, closed Mondays. Across from Recoleta Cemetery. Slots cleanly into Sunday late-afternoon if energy is high.
  • Recoleta Cemetery — Junín 1760. Foreigner admission ~ARS 24,000 (~USD 22), card only at the gate. Buenos Aires Free Walks runs a tip-based 3:30 PM English tour Mon–Sat. Could slot into any free afternoon.
  • Fundación PROA · Penumbra — Dia Art Foundation show (Turrell, Felix Gonzalez-Torres, Agnes Martin) in La Boca. Closes August 2, 2026 — could swap into Sunday afternoon in place of MALBA, or skip.
  • La Viruta Tango — late-night milonga in Palermo, beginner-friendly. Wednesday is the busiest night.
  • Brazilian side of Iguazú — different perspective on the falls. Requires a Brazil eVisa for US citizens (~$80, ~72-hour approval) — start the application this week if including.
